# STX Downloader: full reference

> A Windows app that saves media you're allowed to keep, from YouTube and from web pages, tells you what the audio really is, and plays your whole collection with VLC's engine. Open source under the MIT license, published by Strategia-X (Rocky Elsalaymeh).

Project page: https://git-rocky-stack.github.io/STX-Downloader/
Source: https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader

DRM is out of scope: pages that use DRM get no Save button, and STX doesn't save or play DRM media. You're responsible for each site's terms and the law where you live.

## Save

- Paste a link and yt-dlp handles it, single items and playlists. A playlist asks first.
- Video isn't re-encoded by default: the original streams, in MP4 when they fit and MKV when they don't.
- A Chrome and Edge extension captures HLS, DASH and direct media from a page.

## Check

- Source Truth measures the saved file's audio: spectrum, roll-off, loudness and true peak.
- It gives a plain verdict for each output format, and never says re-encoding improved anything.

## Play

- STX plays media with VLC's engine: the official VLC 3.0.24 build, pinned by sha256, with the parts that would open network ports or run site scripts left out.
- 120 types, each proven by a corpus file.
- Unencrypted DVD and Blu-ray, streams and internet radio. Encrypted discs are refused.
- BIT-PERFECT, a Settings switch, off by default, sends lossless music to your sound device at the file's own rate and depth.
- ENHANCE on the Player: OFF, SHARPEN or UPSCALE, for the picture on screen only. UPSCALE is offered only where the GPU has super resolution.

## Library and Shrink

- The Library holds what you saved, files you opened with STX, and your Videos and Music folders. Removing a row never removes a file.
- SHRINK makes a smaller AV1 or HEVC copy with Opus sound, kept only after it checks out. The original is only read.

## Is it safe?

- The setup and the app's own files are signed through Azure Artifact Signing.
- It installs for your account only, with no administrator prompt.
- The setup brings yt-dlp, FFmpeg and Deno, each checked against its publisher's checksum, so its first launch downloads nothing and works offline. The zip carries the app alone, and its first launch downloads the tools.
- The browser hand-off uses a named pipe only your Windows account can open, and opens no network port.
- Stream tokens, cookies and headers stay in memory, and are scrubbed from the log you can copy.
- Open source, under the MIT license.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 version 2004 or later, x64.
- About 400 MB for the app, and about 430 MB for its tools.
- No runtime to install first: .NET and the Windows App SDK ship inside the app.

## Download, version 1.2.0

- Setup: STXDownloader-1.2.0-setup.exe, 254 MB, SHA-256 1E067230272C7223E1A9430E0B9BFF8E3ADF8C8666477CB2323C2592E7590363
  https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader/releases/download/v1.2.0/STXDownloader-1.2.0-setup.exe
- Portable zip: STXDownloader-1.2.0-win-x64.zip, 171 MB, SHA-256 FEAF84A7A1CE1168F31DB827D637F42745886DB1AFF17DA30DFA86BAB53308F1
  https://github.com/Git-Rocky-Stack/STX-Downloader/releases/download/v1.2.0/STXDownloader-1.2.0-win-x64.zip
- To check a download, run Get-FileHash .\STXDownloader-1.2.0-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256 in PowerShell and compare.

## Install

1. Run the setup. It installs for your account only.
2. Wait for the light at the top right to turn green and read ENGINE CURRENT.
3. Copy a video's link, then press PASTE on the Source plate.

## Tested

On a Core Ultra 7 258V laptop: Arc 140V graphics, a 2880x1800 panel at 175%, HDR on.

- Proven: BIT-PERFECT at 44.1 and 96 kHz on a real sound device; UPSCALE running on the Arc's super resolution; a high-DPI screen; HDR10 reaching an HDR screen as HDR; Default Apps as Windows past 24H2 reads them.
- Not yet: the reference PC's runs of the 50,000-row memory budget, the screenshot gate and the corpus gate; a bit comparison through a hardware loopback; a USB DAC unplugged mid-play; real DVD and Blu-ray discs; film passthrough to a receiver; an RTX GPU; and a clean machine for the installer.
- Known: 4K60 on the laptop's panel loses 3 to 4 pictures a second in about half of the runs. What limits it is VLC 3.0.24's Direct3D 11 output, not decoding.

## Build it yourself

Needs the .NET 10 SDK, Node 24 for the extension's tests, and PowerShell 7.

    dotnet build src/Stx.App -c Release -p:Platform=x64
    dotnet test --project tests/Stx.Core.Tests
    node --test "extension/test/*.test.js"
    tools\Publish.ps1
